newsitem.title: INDIA: India BSE suspends trade in Bank of Baroda shrs.
newsitem.headline: India BSE suspends trade in Bank of Baroda shrs.

text.p: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Friday it had suspended trading in full and partly-paid shares of the state-run Bank of Baroda.
"Due to confusion arising from continuous listing of fully-paid and partly-paid shares, transactions have been suspended," BSE said in an announcement to brokers, minutes after the share was listed.
Bank of Baroda's partly-paid shares of 50 rupees were trading at 35 rupees. Fully-paid shares were trading at 82 rupees, after hitting an early low of 28 rupees.
Brokers said early trade was confused as most investors were unsure which price quotes reflected the shares they held. Both shares listed at 35 rupee levels.
A BSE official told Reuters there would be no trading in the shares on Friday.
In its initial public offer last December, Bank of Baroda issued 100 million shares of 10 rupees face value at 85 rupees a share.
For retail investors, employees and banks, Bank of Baroda collected 25 rupees on application and 25 rupees on allotment. The balance will be collected later in the year.
Shares issued to non-resident Indians, overseas corporate bodies and foreign institutional investors were fully-paid shares at 85 rupees each.
